Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 6) demonstrates a small, hypoplastic right lung with diffuse opacity and marked dextroposition (rightward shift) of the heart and mediastinum, which are hallmark features of Scimitar syndrome (hypogenetic lung syndrome). While the "scimitar" vein itself is best visualized on the CT scans (Figures 4 and 5), Option B correctly describes the characteristic plain film appearance of the affected right hemithorax.
